★★★★☆ Good enough to keep

I paid $38 for this used mechanical keyboard, and I'll say up front that it isn't perfect. The space bar rattles, especially when I hit it with my thumb near the edge. It sounds a bit like a loose pen cap inside a drawer. Also, the "E" key occasionally repeats itself, so every few hundred words I end up with "eexample" or "meeeting" and have to go back and fix it.

Still, I keep reaching for it. The typing feel is lovely: a firm, springy touch that doesn't tire my hands, and the slightly sculpted keycaps suit me well. I answer a lot of email, sometimes for two or three hours at a stretch, and this board has made that far less of a chore than my old membrane keyboard.

The seller was slow. I asked what kind of switches it used, and the reply arrived a full week later, long after I'd worked it out by pulling off a keycap. I considered returning it, but shipping would have cost a chunk of what I paid, and I'd gotten used to the feel by then.

For the price, I'm happy. Just don't expect flawless.

Thirty-eight bucks, used, no box, and a faint smell like somebody else's basement. I knew what I was signing up for. Mostly.

The space bar rattles. Not dramatically, but every time I hit it there's this little tin-can shiver that makes me think a screw is loose somewhere. (I checked. No screws are loose. It's just the stabilizer being a jerk.) And the "L" key occasionally repeats itself, so sometimes I send emails that say "hellllo" with all the confidence of a man who doesn't proofread. It happens maybe once an hour. Annoying, not fatal.

Here's the thing, though: my hands like it. I write a lot of long, dull emails, the kind with bullet points and apologies, and after two hours on this thing my wrists feel fine. The key travel is deep and a little springy, and the typing sound is a soft, low thock rather than a clack. Pleasant.

I asked the seller what switches were inside. He answered a week later. A week! By then I'd already guessed browns, and he said "browns," so, thanks, I guess.

Returning it would've meant a box, tape, a trip to the post office. I kept it. Honestly, I'd probably buy it again, rattle and all.

I paid $38 for this used mechanical keyboard, and I'm keeping it, though not without complaints.

The space bar rattles. Every press produces a hollow clatter, like a pencil dropped in a tin cup, and I hear it most during quiet evening typing. I haven't opened the keyboard to check the stabilizer, so I can't say whether it's a loose wire or just worn plastic.

The other flaw is the "k" key. Maybe once or twice an hour it repeats itself, so "okay" becomes "okkkay." It never happens when I'm watching for it. I've learned to scan each paragraph before sending anything.

What kept me from returning it is how it feels over a long session. I wrote forty emails in one afternoon, and my wrists didn't ache. The keys have enough travel that I stop pressing hard, and the board sits flat without needing a wrist rest.

I asked the seller which switches were inside. The answer came a week later, long after I'd stopped waiting, and it was a single line naming a switch type. By then I had already decided to keep it.

For $38, the noise and the stuttering are annoying but livable. The comfort is real, and it's why this thing stays on my desk.

★★★★☆ Keeping it

The space bar rattles. Hit it with the edge of your thumb and it sounds like a loose pen cap in a drawer. The E key also repeats now and then, so "example" becomes "eexample" and I have to backspace. It happens maybe once an afternoon, always when I'm typing fast and not looking.

I paid $38 and kept it anyway, because of the switches. When I asked the seller what they were, the answer took a week. By then I had already pulled off a keycap and found out for myself: brown tactile switches, with a small bump under the finger and a soft landing at the bottom. My old membrane board felt like pressing wet cardboard by comparison.

My job is mostly email, often two or three hours in a row, and my wrists don't ache by the end anymore. That mattered more than the rattle.

Sending it back would have meant paying for postage and boxing it up, and I'd have been without a keyboard while I waited. So it stays on the desk, and I tap the space bar a little closer to the middle now.
